breaking.headline: Dow turns positive as Wall Street erases most of the rout
breaking.fact: The Dow turned positive by about 2 p.m. ET, up roughly 0.5%, after losing more than 1,100 points at the morning low; the S&P 500 cut a 3.2% plunge to about 0.3% and the Nasdaq trimmed a 4.6% drop to under 1% as bargain hunters stepped in after the hot inflation data.

breaking.headline: Beige Book: growth continues, inflation sticky as December hike looms
breaking.fact: Eight of the Fed's 12 districts grew slightly to moderately in recent weeks while prices kept rising moderately, the Fed's Beige Book showed Wednesday; firms said tariff, energy and healthcare costs are outpacing what they can pass on, and a December rate hike is now nearly certain.

breaking.headline: Trump unveils new tariffs on 14 trading partners
breaking.fact: The administration proposed new Section 301 tariffs on 14 economies including China, the EU and Japan, with China capped at 20% if the trade truce holds and 40% if it fails; duties would not take effect before a January 25 public hearing, likely February at the earliest.

breaking.headline: Jobless claims hit a 4-month low as new home sales jump
breaking.fact: Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 last week, the lowest in four months and well under the 200,000 expected, while October new home sales surged 14.2% to a 701,000 annual rate, a 10-month high. Both prints came in the same 8:30 AM data flurry as the hot PCE report.

watchlist.name: Air Liquide
watchlist.blurb: Air Liquide closed in Paris at €188.46, worth $206.08 at the ECB's Nov 25 reference rate of 1.0935, a small gain on a wild day for U.S. stocks. The industrial-gas giant's defensive profile keeps doing its quiet work while tech craters, with the dollar price tracking the euro near the top of its range. No company news today; the euro's hold above 1.09 is the thing to watch into the holiday.

watchlist.name: Anthropic
watchlist.blurb: Anthropic bounced 3.3% to $84.57, climbing back above its $83 IPO price as the afternoon rally lifted AI names off their lows. The stock had fallen every session since its debut as investors questioned debt-fueled AI spending, and today's hot core PCE reading hardened December hike bets. Sean's IPO allocation is back in the green, barely. Watch whether $83 now holds as support into the holiday break.

watchlist.name: SPDR Bloomberg 1-3 Mo T-Bill
watchlist.blurb: BIL edged up to $91.64 as Treasury bills keep paying: the distribution yield sits at 4.04% with the last payout of $0.30849 per share paid Nov 5. On a day when stocks swung 3% peak to trough, the fund's near-cash profile is exactly why Sean holds it as the portfolio's anchor. It will keep inching higher a few cents a month. Watch the December Fed decision for the yield path.

watchlist.name: Alphabet
watchlist.blurb: Alphabet fell 2.4% to $272.38 as the AI selloff spread from chips to the hyperscalers, though the stock is well off its morning lows after the afternoon bounce. Hot October core PCE at 3.3% hardened bets on a December Fed hike, lifting the discount rate on growth names. GOOGL remains one of Sean's core long-term winners despite the drawdown. Watch whether it holds $270 into the Thanksgiving break.

watchlist.name: Eli Lilly
watchlist.blurb: Eli Lilly slipped 0.7% to $1,397.59, a mild dip on a wild tape after Tuesday's 3.2% jump on the Moody's upgrade to Aa2. The drugmaker's diabetes and weight-loss franchises remain the growth engine, and healthcare held up far better than tech today as investors rotated to defensives. The drop looks like holiday de-risking, not a thesis change. Watch for buyers to step back in after Thanksgiving.

watchlist.name: Cheniere Energy
watchlist.blurb: Cheniere rose 1.8% to $301.37, one of the day's green names as energy rallied on the Hormuz mine strikes and the Houthi claim on Ras Tanura. Brent eased back toward $90 in the afternoon, but LNG exporters held their gains on firm export demand and long-term contracts. Cheniere's contracted volumes insulate it from spot swings. Watch the OPEC+ meeting Sunday for the next supply signal.

watchlist.name: Nvidia
watchlist.blurb: Nvidia slid 4.7% to $148.11, leading the chip rout as the AI trade unwound again after Monday's reinstatement rally. Hot core PCE cemented a December hike, and tariff headlines added to the doubt over AI spending that has dogged the sector all month. Sean's call stands: a long-term hold until the probes shake out. The Dec 1 House testimony is the next checkpoint to watch.

watchlist.name: Pfizer
watchlist.blurb: Pfizer was flat at $28.43, holding up far better than the growth names as investors rotated toward defensives. The dividend payer had jumped 3.9% Tuesday and stays near the top of its recent range, its yield cushioning the tape. Sean holds it for income as much as growth. Watch for any pipeline or guidance news into year-end; the dividend above 6% keeps income buyers patient.

watchlist.name: Rocket Lab
watchlist.blurb: Rocket Lab rose 2.7% to $47.21, bouncing with the afternoon rally after a steep morning slide with speculative growth names. The space stock has given back much of its autumn run in the November risk-off wave, with no company news behind the swings. Sean holds it as an aggressive-growth bet, so sharp moves are part of the deal. Watch whether $45 holds as support into the holiday.

watchlist.name: Rithm Capital
watchlist.blurb: Rithm Capital jumped 3.2% to $8.95, one of the day's strongest watchlist names as mortgage REITs benefited from falling Treasury yields. The 10-year slipped to 4.84% after the data, easing pressure on Rithm's book and its dividend story. The stock has climbed steadily off its lows this month as spreads improved. Watch the December Fed decision, which sets the tone for mortgage spreads.

watchlist.name: SpaceX
watchlist.blurb: SPCX rose 1.2% to $127.38, recovering with the afternoon bounce after a steep morning slide. The de-SPAC fund tracks former SPACs, the market's most sentiment-sensitive corner, so it swings hard with the tape in both directions. Sharp reversals are the norm here. It remains an aggressive-growth holding for Sean. Watch for stabilization once the Thanksgiving break resets sentiment.

watchlist.name: Truist Financial
watchlist.blurb: Truist rose 1.0% to $47.94, a modest gain as banks held up better than tech in the selloff and joined the afternoon bounce. The regional lender benefits from a steeper curve and steady credit, and its dividend keeps income investors patient through the volatility. Today's move is mostly tape-driven, not Truist-specific. Watch the December Fed hike decision and any loan-growth commentary.

watchlist.name: U.S. Antimony
watchlist.blurb: U.S. Antimony edged up 0.9% to $2.20, steadying after the morning selloff as the broader tape bounced. The stock had re-armed the bottom watch off its lows, and holding $2.00 keeps that thesis alive into the holiday. Antimony's DOD and supply-chain case is unchanged by a day's tape. Watch whether $2.20 holds into the holiday; the bottom watch stays armed for the next signal.

watchlist.name: Uranium Energy
watchlist.blurb: Uranium Energy rose 2.4% to $5.71, bouncing with the tape after Tuesday's slide erased last week's surge off the $5.30 low. The long-term nuclear story — reactor restarts, SMR approvals, government buying — is intact, but speculative names are whipsawing with the market on tariff and rate headlines. Sean wants to add while prices are low. Watch for a hold above $5.50 into the holiday.

watchlist.name: Valero Energy
watchlist.blurb: Valero was flat at $324.66 even as crude rallied, with refiners lagging the oil move as the market frets over margins and demand. Brent near $90 would normally lift the complex, but today's risk-off tape hit the energy patch except the producers, and refining cracks stayed soft. Valero remains a locked long-term hold for Sean. Watch crack spreads and the OPEC+ decision Sunday.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Target 2035
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard Target Retirement 2035 held at $28.43, its Nov 24 NAV, with no new price until tonight's close. The balanced fund's bond sleeve cushioned today's equity slide, doing exactly what a target-date fund is built to do on a day the Nasdaq fell 4% before bouncing. Sean holds it as a steady core position, not a trading vehicle. Watch tonight's NAV for the full read on the selloff.

watchlist.name: VI5TC (est.)
watchlist.blurb: The S&P 500-anchored estimate slipped 0.3% to $147.57 as the index gave back most of the morning's plunge by the afternoon. The estimate tracks the S&P 500 from the $155.58 anchor set Nov 3, so it mirrors the market's wild swing almost exactly. It remains a work-related holding Sean cannot trade. Watch whether the index can hold above 7,150 into the Thanksgiving break.

watchlist.name: Schwab Value Advantage MF
watchlist.blurb: Schwab's money fund holds at $1.00 with a 7-day yield of 3.78%, published Nov 24. The sweep vehicle keeps earning while stocks swing, and per Sean's plan any balance over $1,000 in an account gets sold for a CD. The position should keep evaporating over time. Watch the December Fed hike, which would nudge the yield higher; any hike flows straight through to money funds.

watchlist.name: Vanguard Treasury MMF
watchlist.blurb: Vanguard's Treasury money fund holds at $1.00 with a 7-day SEC yield of 4.04%, published Nov 24. It remains the top-yielding cash parking spot in the lineup, beating SWVXX by 26 basis points, and the home for Sean's Treasury cash at eTrade. The yield tracks the Fed's path closely and the fund owns only Treasuries, so there is no credit risk. Watch the December hike decision for the next move.

weekInBrief.headline: Consumer confidence jumps to 103.3, highest in nearly two years
weekInBrief.body: The Conference Board's consumer confidence index surged 11.4 points to 103.3 in November, far above the 92.4 forecast and its highest since January 2025, as Americans' view of the economy brightened despite sticky inflation. Strong consumers leave the Fed little reason to pause, keeping a December hike nearly certain.

weekInBrief.headline: Anthropic claws back above its $83 IPO price
weekInBrief.body: Anthropic rose 3.3% to $84.57 on Wednesday, reclaiming its $83 IPO price as the afternoon rally lifted AI names off their morning lows. The stock had fallen every session since its debut last Thursday as investors questioned whether debt-fueled AI spending will pay off. The IPO allocation is back in the green — barely.

weekInBrief.headline: U.S. crude stocks build 1.1 million barrels, less than expected
weekInBrief.body: EIA data showed U.S. crude inventories rose 1.11 million barrels last week, below the 2.0 million-barrel build analysts expected, as the Hormuz standoff kept supply risk in focus. The smaller-than-expected build adds to the case that the market is tighter than surplus forecasts suggest.

weekInBrief.headline: Mortgage applications jump 6.1% as buyers return
weekInBrief.body: Mortgage applications rose 6.1% in the week ended Nov 20, the MBA said, with the purchase index up 10.2% as buyers stepped back in. The rebound pairs with October's strong new home sales and suggests housing demand is stirring despite high rates. Refinancing was flat, up just 0.5%.

items.headline: Latest from the Strait
items.body: Two more oil tankers struck naval mines and caught fire in the Strait on Wednesday morning, the IRGC Navy said — the latest in a near-daily run of attacks, with the claim unverified and the vessels unnamed. Tehran's parliament speaker set seven conditions for talks, including lifting the U.S. naval blockade and sanctions relief; Washington rejected the terms, and CENTCOM launched Task Force Iron Gate to disrupt weapons and sanctioned-material flows across Iran's land borders and Caspian ports. A Houthi missile hit a commercial skyscraper in Riyadh, injuring 11, while the Saudi-led coalition destroyed four attack drones over the Ras Tanura export complex. Iranian crude is still not getting past the blockade — Kpler now puts Iranian oil on the water outside the blockade zone at zero, with the 40 to 50 million barrels already in Asia discharging in China at close to 1 million barrels a day — while non-Iranian Gulf oil keeps flowing at roughly 70% of pre-war volumes, though flows have slipped in recent days as the attacks continue.

space.headline: Hera's first images show a stadium-size crater on Dimorphos
space.body: The European Space Agency's Hera spacecraft has released its first images of Dimorphos, the asteroid NASA's DART mission struck in 2022: a stadium-size crater that flattened one of the rock's rounded faces, and hundreds of previously unknown boulders — more than 100 between the size of a football and a washing machine — encircling the asteroid pair. Hera arrived three weeks ago and is flying about 30 km from the binary asteroid system. The survey will refine the deflection techniques that could one day protect Earth.

space.headline: Webb finds the farthest 'little red dot' yet
space.body: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope have found the most distant 'little red dot' yet — CW-LRD-z10, a candidate early supermassive black hole seen 400 to 500 million years after the Big Bang. The team combined Webb's NIRCam and MIRI instruments to pin the distance, confirmed by spectroscopy showing the Lyman-alpha break. The find, published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, pushes the hunt for the universe's first black holes further back.

space.headline: St. Jude cracks precise DNA integration with engineered CAST system
space.body: St. Jude scientists have uncovered how CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs) integrate DNA at precise genomic targets, publishing the structural work in Nature today. The team redesigned the type I-F3 CAST to work 100 times more efficiently without losing its on-target specificity — a step toward programming DNA insertion where you want it in a genome. The findings give genomic engineering a mechanistic framework it lacked.

space.headline: Selenium isotopes map the hidden plate-tectonic cycle
space.body: An international team has traced the missing link in Earth's plate-tectonic cycle, showing how subducted crust reacts with the mantle, preserves its chemical fingerprint for hundreds of millions of years, and rises to melt beneath mid-ocean ridges. Using selenium isotopes and numerical modeling, published in Science Advances, they found less than 10% recycled material in the mantle source drives the observed isotopic shift — quantifying deep-Earth mass transfer for the first time.

apod.title: Eye of the Sahara
apod.explanation: The Richat Structure, also known as the "Eye of the Sahara," is seen from the International Space Station as it orbited above on Nov. 14, 2026. It is an eroded geological dome about 100 million years old created by igneous activity and uplift in Mauritania. In this type of geologic structure, rocks exposed in the center of the "bullseye" are older than rocks forming the outer rings. This structure measures 45 kilometers (28 miles) across and is made up of igneous and sedimentary rocks.
